title: JUnit and JVM Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of junit and jvm testing using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates junit and jvm testing.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **JUnit and JVM Testing** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks. Use the subtopics—Organizing JUnit Tests, Testing Exceptions, Running Tests Through Gradle—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

items.title: Organizing JUnit Tests
items.text: Organizing JUnit Tests helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: JUnit and JVM Testing removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
